explanation: Fires on a '0' digit token inside a run of zeros, especially the zero after '0.0'/'0.00' in p-values (P < 0.001), hex constants (0x00000, #000) and zero-padded numbers like 43,000; strongest when preceded by '00' or '0.0'. A few non-digit word-piece tokens (e.g. 'ORE' in SOPHOMORE, 'e' in oboe) also fire, and other digits fire only weakly.

Fires on the head noun or relativizer right after a determiner or modifier that opens a defining phrase, most of all 'invention' in the patent boilerplate 'The present invention relates to', and also 'that' in 'the forum that / a way that', 'Policy', 'motto', 'word'. Ordinary nouns and conjunctions in running text fire only weakly.

Mixed, mostly code or technical tokens: 'Software' in 'Distributed under the Boost Software License', version-number dots (TLSv1.2, 0.23, 1.0.2), type-annotation separators (' :', ' ->', '}{') and LaTeX pieces, plus scattered prose tokens. No single context predicts it well.

Fires on a generic noun that comes right after a determiner or adjective and names the item being introduced or referred to (a link, this link, two passes, a family, the following statements, error code, this trigger, common proofs). It is strongest in technical, Q&A or scientific prose where the noun is a general category word.

Fires on the token just after a slash, or a domain-suffix token, in paths, URLs, include paths and slash-joined pairs ('clang/', 'Zend/Pdf', '18/07', 'MUM1/IRF4', 'location/expansion', 'wikimedia.org/'). The slash-joined piece itself carries the activation, and it is strongest in include/require paths and A/B compounds.

Mixture: interior zeros of long zero strings ('00000000'), mid-word pieces of technical or biomedical terms (-ocyte, -ovolta-, -renal-, Nitro-, Glibc), '-Version' in 'MIME-Version', and 'FROM' in license text. These share no clear common feature.

Fires on an opening parenthesis ' (' (with a space before it) that follows a noun phrase in prose and starts an aside: birth dates after a biography name, 'e.g.', 'i.e.', abbreviations, or license clauses like '(INCLUDING' and '(the "Software")'. Parentheses in code or math, with no space before them, fire only weakly.

Fires on the copula, auxiliary or pronoun that comes after an explanation or causal frame and points to what follows, such as 'is' in 'the reason is', 'was' in 'the error was', 'it's because', 'not sure if', 'this was'. It is strongest in speculative or explanatory sentences ('I assume it's', 'the answer is').

Mostly fires on abstract nouns completing a fixed collocation after an adjective: 'safety/security/environmental concerns', 'aspects' (biological/molecular/important aspect), 'importance' (critical importance). Weaker hits include 'one of', 'has been', and CJK particles (给, は).

Mixed: 'by' in 'Created by / Written by', 'appeal(s)' in legal opinions ('This appeal', 'X appeals from'), 'to/us/you' after contact or writing verbs, plus random pieces of words and numbers in patents and medical terms.

Fires on word pieces in the middle of words in non-English, mostly European languages (Turkish, German, Romanian, Czech, French, Portuguese), as well as Latin taxonomic names and some medical words ('echocardiography'). It is a sub-word continuation detector for foreign or unusual words.

Fires on Spanish, Portuguese or Italian text (word pieces inside Romance words) and on Hispanic or Latin-American names in English, especially 'Angeles' in 'Los Angeles', 'Mexican', 'Argentina', 'San Diego'. Unrelated English tokens are weak.

Fires on the first token of a new sentence or statement right after a break: 'I' that opens a post or question body ('Q: ... title ... I have'), 'if' at the start of a shell or GN line, and tokens right after 'v.' in case captions. It responds to statement-initial position after a heading or line break, with the pronoun 'I' being most common.

Heterogeneous: unit 'D' (diopters), 'DISTRICT' in court headers, '0' in '#sec001' section anchors, '.read', 'Console', 'Photo' in AP credits, and many suffix pieces of technical words. No common feature.

Mixed code and technical pieces: underscore-prefixed identifier pieces (O_NONBLOCK, m_Double, _open, JSC_J), 'bur' in 'outbursts', 'ol' in phospholipid, the article 'a/be' in license text, and colons in error messages. No clear single function.

Mixed: 'charset' and 'meta' in HTML/HTTP Content-Type headers, method or package names in code (decodeURIComponent, UnityEditor, inflate, MustCompile, apimachinery), and some English words ('outpatient', 'internationally', 'overshadowed', 'Anaheim').

Fires on a middle word piece of a long, mostly Latinate English word that is split into several tokens, such as intr-INS-ically, irreconc-IL-able, ab-OMIN-able, eup-HEM-istically, ag-GLOMER-ates, syn-CRET-ic. The activation depends on being an interior subword of a rare multi-token word.

Fires on an adjective (often ending in -al/-ical/-ic) that modifies a following noun to form a technical or institutional compound term: 'operational amplifier', 'cosmic microwave', 'planetary protection', 'numerical transfer', 'Statistical Science', 'judicial release', 'Medical marijuana'. The token is the classifying adjective of a noun compound.

Mixed: the leading ' *' on blank-then-continued lines of C-style license comment blocks, nouns in hardware or storage contexts (disk, shift register, plurality, chamber reference numbers), 'Bankrupt', 'security', and 'in' in shell for-loops.

Fires on a discourse connective that adds a narrowing or alternative, most strongly 'more' in the patent boilerplate 'relates to X and, more particularly/specifically, to Y'. Also fires on 'or', 'except' and 'but' that begin a parenthetical alternative or qualification ('(or at least', ', or similar').

Fires on words about soil, compost and nutrient or agricultural ecology: humus, compost, humic, soil, litter, peat, fertilizers, nutrient cycling, nitrogen, phosphate, organic matter, sludge. Strength drops off with distance from the soil or compost meaning.
